issues.title: Unsafe block lacks safety documentation
issues.description: The rule requires unsafe code blocks to include comprehensive comments explaining why the code is safe, what invariants must be maintained, and under what conditions the code is valid. This unsafe block uses mem::zeroed() and calls libc::ioctl() without documenting the safety invariants.
issues.rule_name: Unsafe Code Must Include Safety Documentation

issues.title: Missing tauri_dir parameter causes workspace resolution to use wrong directory
issues.description: The `get_workspace_dir()` function is called without the required `tauri_dir` parameter in `cargo_manifest_and_lock()`. This function now requires `tauri_dir` to correctly resolve the workspace directory after the refactoring. Without it, the code will fail to compile since `get_workspace_dir()` signature was changed to require a `&Path` parameter throughout the codebase. This breaks the Cargo.lock resolution logic which is critical for determining package versions and dependencies.

issues.title: Configuration merge bypasses validation when merging with empty configs
issues.description: The `merge_config_with` function returns early with `Ok(())` when `merge_configs.is_empty()`, but this skips critical validation and state updates that should occur even when no merge is performed. The original code in `merge_with` returned the handle, maintaining the contract that callers could safely use the config. This early return can cause downstream code to operate on stale or unvalidated configuration state, particularly affecting build and dev commands that rely on properly initialized config metadata.

issues.title: Missing directory parameter breaks WiX upgrade code validation
issues.description: In `wix_settings`, the environment variable check `std::env::var_os("TAURI_BUNDLER_WIX_FIPS_COMPLIANT")` was changed but the subsequent check incorrectly compares `OsString` with a string literal "true". The original code used `std::env::var()` which returns a `String`, but `var_os()` returns `OsString` which cannot be directly compared with `==` against a string slice. This breaks FIPS compliance detection for WiX installers, potentially creating non-compliant Windows builds when FIPS mode is required.

issues.title: New public struct and function lack rustdoc comments
issues.description: `Dirs` and `resolve_dirs` are newly introduced public API items but have no `///` documentation comments as required.
issues.rule_name: Rule 7: Public APIs Must Include Documentation Comments

issues.title: New public config functions lack rustdoc comments
issues.description: The newly introduced public functions `get_config`, `reload_config`, and `merge_config_with` have no `///` documentation comments, violating the requirement that public APIs be documented.
issues.rule_name: Rule 7: Public APIs Must Include Documentation Comments

issues.title: New/modified path resolution introduces panics/unwraps for fallible operations
issues.description: `resolve_dirs` uses `panic!` and `unwrap()` (`tauri.parent().unwrap()`) for fallible operations (project discovery/path parent resolution) instead of returning a `Result`, violating the rule to make failure explicit rather than panicking.
issues.rule_name: Rule 16: Functions Should Return Result Types for Fallible Operations

pr.title: Code Review Bench PR #14668 - Less statics
pr.author: unknown

structured_output.summary:
This refactor removes the process-wide `Mutex<Option<ConfigMetadata>>` config handle and the `tauri_dir()`/`frontend_dir()` accessors from `tauri-cli`. Callers now receive a `Dirs { tauri, frontend }` value from `app_paths::resolve_dirs()` and an owned `ConfigMetadata` from `config::get_config`, and pass them down explicitly. Reloads on file change go through `reload_config(&mut ConfigMetadata, ...)`, and the dev/mobile paths share config through a `Mutex` that is local to each command. The direction is sound and the change is mostly mechanical. Most of the churn is signature plumbing through build, bundle, dev, and the Android and iOS paths.

The main problem is a likely compile error in `dev.rs`: a non-`move` closure passed to `std::thread::spawn` borrows the `&Dirs` parameter, which the spawn's `'static` bound rejects. There are also a few smaller issues. An unrelated `features` default changed in the iOS config, several drive-by edits are bundled into a refactor PR, and a Mutex guard is held across the whole Android build. I could not run `cargo check` in this environment, so the compile finding is based on reading the code and on Rust's closure-capture rules rather than on a build.
structured_output.verdictRationale: The `thread::spawn` in `dev::setup` most likely fails to compile, which blocks the whole crate. The iOS `features` default change is an unexplained behaviour change inside a refactor. The remaining items are low-risk cleanups. Once the spawn is fixed and the iOS change is reverted or justified, this looks mergeable.

architecture.overview:
Before this PR, `tauri-cli` kept two process-wide `OnceLock<PathBuf>` values (tauri dir and frontend dir) and a `static Mutex<Option<ConfigMetadata>>` config handle. Any module could reach them through `app_paths::tauri_dir()`, `frontend_dir()`, and `config::get`/`reload`/`merge_with`. Every access then went through `lock().unwrap().as_ref().unwrap()`, and a missing `resolve()` or config load panicked at runtime.

The PR moves ownership to the entry points. Each command calls `app_paths::resolve_dirs()` once and gets a `Dirs { tauri: &'static Path, frontend: &'static Path }`. It then calls `config::get_config(target, merges, tauri_dir)` to get an owned `ConfigMetadata`. That value is passed by reference into `AppInterface::new`, `build::setup`, `bundle::bundle`, and the mobile builders. Dev and mobile-dev wrap the config in a local `Mutex` so the file watcher can call `reload_config(&mut config.lock(), ...)`. The `&'static` fields in `Dirs` still point into the `OnceLock` globals, so the statics are reduced but not removed.
steps: Entry point: each `command()` in `lib.rs`, `dev.rs`, `build.rs`, `bundle.rs`, `mobile/*` now calls `app_paths::resolve_dirs()` instead of `resolve()` followed by global accessors. `resolve_dirs` lazily initialises the two `OnceLock`s and returns `Dirs`.

Config load: `config::get_config(target, merges, tauri_dir)` parses `tauri.conf.json` and returns an owned `ConfigMetadata`. `reload_config` replaces it in place only after a successful load, and `merge_config_with` merges CLI `--config` overrides.
Interface plumbing: `Interface::new/build/dev/mobile_dev/watch` and `AppSettings::out_dir/get_binaries/get_bundler_settings` now take `tauri_dir` or `dirs` explicitly instead of reading the global.

Dev watcher: `Rust::run_dev_watcher` receives `&Mutex<ConfigMetadata>`. On a configuration-file change it calls `reload_config` and then `rewrite_manifest(&config, dirs.tauri)`. This replaces the old global reload with a per-command mutable value.

Mobile paths: Android and iOS `build`, `dev`, `run`, `init`, and `xcode_script` each load their own `ConfigMetadata`. Dev and run share it through a local `Mutex` passed into `mobile_dev`/`watch`. `init` and `xcode_script` use the same `get_config` call, and `build::setup` now takes `dirs`.

findings.title: `thread::spawn` closure borrows `dirs`, so the crate likely won't compile
findings.fixPrompt: In `crates/tauri-cli/src/dev.rs`, `setup()` (around lines 138-148) spawns a thread whose non-`move` closure reads `dirs.frontend` and `dirs.tauri` from the `&Dirs` parameter. That borrows a non-'static value and `std::thread::spawn` will not compile. Copy the two `&'static Path` fields into local bindings before the spawn and change the closure to `move`. Keep the existing `check_mismatched_packages` call and its `log::error!` handling unchanged. This restores the behaviour the old global accessors gave for free.

findings.title: iOS `features` default changed without explanation
findings.fixPrompt: In `crates/tauri-cli/src/mobile/ios/mod.rs` inside `get_config` (around line 272), `ApplePlatform.features` was changed from `if ios_options.features.is_empty() { None } else { Some(ios_options.features) }` to an unconditional `Some(ios_options.features)`. This is unrelated to the statics refactor. Restore the original conditional so that an empty feature list yields `None`, unless the change is deliberate. If it is deliberate, explain why in the PR description.

findings.title: Mutex guard held across the entire Android build
findings.fixPrompt: In `crates/tauri-cli/src/mobile/android/build.rs`, `run()` (around line 154) locks the Mutex and holds the guard for the whole function. The build path only reads the config, so this guard isn't needed and will deadlock if anything later locks the config during a build. Change `run()` to take `&ConfigMetadata` and do the locking at the call site in `android/run.rs` (where the Mutex is later shared with `watch`). Keep the same behaviour for `run_build`, `ensure_init`, and `build::setup`.

findings.title: Config loaded twice in iOS run path
findings.fixPrompt: In `crates/tauri-cli/src/mobile/ios/run.rs`, `command()` loads the Tauri config again (around line 101) after `build::command` has already loaded it. Have the iOS build path return the `ConfigMetadata` it used, or split `build::command` so the loaded config can be passed back to `run.rs`. Then pass that single config into the `Mutex` used by `watch`. This avoids two reads of `tauri.conf.json` that can diverge.

findings.title: Unrelated drive-by edits bundled into a statics refactor
findings.body:
Several changes have nothing to do with removing statics, and they make the PR harder to review and revert:

- `helpers/config.rs` switches `std::env::var(...).ok()` to `std::env::var_os(...)` for `TAURI_BUNDLER_WIX_FIPS_COMPLIANT`. A non-UTF-8 value that used to fall back to the config now compares as `false`.
- `interface/rust/desktop.rs` deletes the comment explaining the FreeBSD `.into()` on `TIOCGWINSZ`, while keeping the conversion itself.
- `mobile/mod.rs::local_ip_address` rewrites a `match` on `addresses.len()` as a slice pattern. The behaviour is the same, but it is unrelated churn.

::diff{file="crates/tauri-cli/src/helpers/config.rs" lines="71-78"}

Split these into their own PRs, or revert them here.
findings.fixPrompt: This refactor PR contains unrelated edits. In `crates/tauri-cli/src/helpers/config.rs` (around line 74), `wix_settings` changed `std::env::var(...).ok()` to `var_os`, which changes behaviour for non-UTF-8 values. In `crates/tauri-cli/src/interface/rust/desktop.rs` (around line 352), the FreeBSD `.into()` explanatory comment was removed. In `crates/tauri-cli/src/mobile/mod.rs`, `local_ip_address` was rewritten as a slice match. Revert these three changes so the PR only contains the statics refactor, or move them to a separate PR.

findings.title: Redundant nested block in `xcode_script` config loading
findings.body:
`ios/xcode_script.rs` wraps `cli_options` in two nested blocks. The inner `read_options` call is only there to give the outer block a value, and the outer block's shadowing makes the control flow harder to follow. `read_options(&tauri_config)` is also called again a few lines later. The nested block could be flattened to a single `let cli_options = read_options(&tauri_config);` at the top level.

::code{file="crates/tauri-cli/src/mobile/ios/xcode_script.rs" lines="96-102"}
findings.fixPrompt: In `crates/tauri-cli/src/mobile/ios/xcode_script.rs` around lines 97-100, the `cli_options` binding is wrapped in two nested blocks (`let cli_options = { let cli_options = { read_options(&tauri_config) }; ... cli_options };`). Flatten this to one top-level `let cli_options = read_options(&tauri_config);` followed by the `if !cli_options.config.is_empty()` reload. Keep the reload with `reload_tauri_config(&mut tauri_config, ...)` as is.

findings.title: `Dirs` still depends on the statics it was meant to remove
findings.fixPrompt: In `crates/tauri-cli/src/helpers/app_paths.rs`, `Dirs` stores `&'static Path` fields that point into the `FRONTEND_DIR` and `TAURI_DIR` `OnceLock` statics, so the globals are kept. Consider making `Dirs` own `PathBuf` fields and having `resolve_dirs()` return them directly, which removes both `OnceLock`s. Update the callers that take `&Dirs` to borrow from the owned fields. Note that the `thread::spawn` in `dev.rs` is simpler with owned or `'static` data, but it also needs a `move` closure either way.

findings.title: Reload keeps the previous config on failure and drops unwrap panics
findings.fixPrompt: No change needed. This is a positive note on the `reload_config` and watcher code, which keeps the old config on a failed reload and removes the old unwrap panic sites.
